deck: The best sunscreen is the one that ends up on your face every morning.
description: How to choose a daily sunscreen — SPF, texture, and the habit that matters more than the label.

public.body: Sunscreen prevents more visible aging than any serum reverses. And the fanciest formula is worthless in the drawer — the one you enjoy wearing wins.

SPF 30 blocks about 97% of UVB; SPF 50, about 98%. The jump is small, so choose the higher number if it helps you feel covered, but do not agonize. "Broad spectrum" — covering UVA too — matters more than chasing SPF 100.
public.title: What the numbers mean

items: Pick a texture you like — cream, gel, or fluid — so you reach for it daily.
A visible amount: about two finger-lengths for the face and neck.
public.title: How to choose

public.body: Consistency beats perfection. A pleasant SPF 30 worn every day protects far better than an SPF 50 you skip because it feels heavy.
